study_id: Barbosa et al. - 2018 - Machine Learning Algorithms Utilizing Quantitative CT Features May Predict Eventual Onset of Bronchi

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study involves adult lung transplant recipients and uses a non‑linear machine learning model (support vector machine) to predict bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome, an important post‑transplant complication, and was published as a peer‑reviewed article in 2018.

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of paired inspiratory‑expiratory CT scans and pulmonary function tests from 71 lung transplant patients (41 BOS, 30 non‑BOS).
identification_methods.Institution: Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Retrospective clinical CT and PFT data from lung transplant recipients.
identification_methods.Identification Notes: 71 LTx patients with paired inspiratory‑expiratory CT scans; BOS defined by >10% sustained FEV1 decline.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Support Vector Machine with radial basis function kernel (cost=1, gamma=1/feature dimension).
identification_methods.Comparator: Standard clinical parameters (e.g., FEV1) used as reference.
identification_methods.Input Variables: Baseline quantitative CT (qCT) features: imaging lobar volume, airway volume, airway resistance, airway surface, etc.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Scans of poor quality excluded; patients with missing regional parameters were omitted from feature‑selection.
identification_methods.Validation Method: Random training/test splits: 90%/10% for 1‑ and 2‑feature models (500 repetitions), 80%/20% for 3‑feature model (100 repetitions).
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Linear mixed‑effects analysis, Student t tests for individual biomarkers, followed by supervised SVM classification; multiple random partitions used to estimate accuracy.

population.Inclusion criteria: Status post unilateral or bilateral lung transplantation, availability of at least two chest CTs performed ≥3 months apart, pulmonary function testing within 2 weeks of each CT, and volumetric paired inspiratory and expiratory thin-section CTs
population.Exclusion criteria: Poor quality CT scans were excluded
population.Population Notes: Retrospective analysis of paired inspiratory‑expiratory CT scans; 41 patients developed BOS and 30 did not; data include baseline and follow‑up imaging and pulmonary function tests
population.Diagnosis: Pre‑transplant diagnoses: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (26), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (23), cystic fibrosis (7), alpha‑1 antitrypsin deficiency (5), other (10)

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: Support Vector Machine (SVM) with radial basis function kernel
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Quantitative CT (qCT) features from paired inspiratory‑expiratory scans
interventions_outcomes.Number of Predictors: Three qCT parameters used in the final model
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: Student t test to identify significant baseline features, then SVM classification
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Baseline (static) prediction of eventual BOS development
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: SVM models optimized for accuracy; training‑test split of 80%‑20% for three‑feature model, default cost=1 and gamma=1/number of features
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Prediction of eventual bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) development
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Accuracy, sensitivity and specificity reported for SVM classifier
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Focus on SVM performance in classifying BOS developers vs non‑developers
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: Baseline lung transplant patients with complete qCT data (n=41)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Test Set Size: Approximately 8–9 patients (20% of 41) used as test set; total cohort n=41
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Proportion of correctly classified cases (accuracy) on held‑out test set
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: ML using three baseline qCT features predicts eventual BOS with high accuracy
